links.outcome: Exam accuracy with stepwise prompting strategies including retrieval-augmented generation versus baseline
links.effect: All strategies combined (prompt engineering, RAG, five-shot, AVRM) raised GPT-4 from 60.3% to 80.7% and Gemini Pro from 48.0% to 54.3%; RAG-specific effect not given in abstract.
links.quote: Implementing all prompting strategies improved the overall score of GPT-4 from 60.3% to 80.7% and Gemini Pro’s from 48.0% to 54.3%.

links.outcome: Accuracy gain from adding an LLM-powered answer validation revision model to other prompting strategies
links.effect: AVRM added to prompt, RAG and 5-shot increased GPT-4 accuracy by 4.4%.
links.quote: The addition of the AVRM to prompt, RAG and 5-shot increased GPT-4’s accuracy by 4.4%.

unlisted_practices: Prompt engineering and five-shot learning to improve LLM accuracy on subspecialty exam questions

screen.practice: retrieval grounding, prompt engineering, and LLM answer validation
screen.reason: The study tests the stepwise addition of deployment strategies (RAG, few-shot prompting, prompt engineering, and an automated answer validation revision model) to existing multimodal foundation models on a medical specialty board examination.

primary.practice: prompt engineering, RAG, few-shot prompting, and automated answer validation/revision
